main_issue: Who gets to use the single window corner of the living room (shrine, work desk, laundry rack, or friends' seating), and whether a shared or alternative arrangement is possible.

A-B.evidence: B's weekend seating claim (4) conflicts with A; B then proposes timing (8) and asks A about alternatives (25), A refuses to move (26); B's final point (30) is neutral.

A-C.evidence: Both claim the corner for their own need (3, 5, 9) and never address each other; both insist no alternative exists (17, 26).

A-D.evidence: A refuses to give up the desk (1, 3) and acknowledges D's prayer only briefly (7); D says there is no other space (24, 28); no resolution reached.

B-C.evidence: B suggests timing (8) and C rejects it (9); B accepts the point (12) and later concedes laundry has to be there (22), but C is not moved on a shared arrangement.

B-D.evidence: B's friends use the corner (4), but B comes to question alternatives for everyone (16, 20), and B replies to D's complaint at (30) that all would lose if one claims the corner.

C-D.evidence: D says shrine can't be next to laundry (10) and complains about unequal treatment (14); C says there's no other window place (13, 17); neither yields.
